records.title: African Union Commission Internship Programme (Req 1506, Ethiopia, unpaid)
records.overview: Full-time internship of three months, renewable once, at the African Union Commission (job location Ethiopia; the AU headquarters are in Addis Ababa), open to nationals of AU member states who are in the final year of a Bachelor's or hold a Bachelor's or Master's degree in a related field. Prior work experience is not required. Applications go through the AU Careers portal (posting Req 1506, ending 31 December 2026). The AU pays no allowance or travel and the intern covers accommodation, living costs and insurance.
records.city: Addis Ababa (AU headquarters; the posting gives only 'Job Location (country): Ethiopia')
records.program_dates: Three months, renewable one time (AU portal posting). Start date not stated; interns work full time, Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00 (programme FAQ).
records.deadline_text: AU Careers portal posting 'Internship Program' (Req Id 1506): 'Posting Start Date 2/16/26', 'End Date December 31, 2026'. No time or time zone is stated.
funding_details: AU portal posting: 'The AU will have no financial obligation towards interns - travel arrangements and cost of accommodation and living expenses will be the responsibility of the interns.'

Posting: 'AU will use reasonable efforts to assist the interns in obtaining their entry and residence visas' (assistance, no fee coverage stated)

records.stipend: None: the AU pays interns no allowance or per diem

records.title: UNICEF Internship Programme (stipend; vacancies through the year, DRC offices included)
records.overview: UNICEF internships for students and recent graduates, normally six to twenty-six weeks, full or part time and sometimes remote, with a monthly stipend and possibly a one-time lump sum towards travel and visa costs. Each vacancy is advertised on the UNICEF vacancies page with its own deadline, field and duty station; UNICEF's DRC offices (Kinshasa, Goma, Bunia) have advertised internships. Eligibility: enrolled in a degree programme or graduated within the past two years.

records.title: SADC Secretariat Work-Integrated Learning (WIL) programme: interns and graduates (Gaborone and Lusaka)
records.overview: Work-integrated learning placements of three to twelve months at the SADC Secretariat in Gaborone (Botswana) and the SADC Plant Genetic Resource Centre in Lusaka (Zambia) for citizens of SADC member states, a group that includes the Democratic Republic of Congo. The June 2026 call took students and graduates (a graduate must have graduated at least a year before enrolment), set an age limit of under 52, and offered a return ticket and a USD 250 monthly stipend; applications went through each member state's SADC National Contact Point. That call closed on 28 June 2026 and the SADC vacancies page currently lists no vacancy.

records.program_dates: June 2026 call: internship opportunities of not less than three months and graduate opportunities of a fixed period of not less than twelve months; start dates not stated.
records.deadline_text: Closed. records.title: EAC Youth Fellowship (MS TCDC, Arusha): 4th cohort closed 7 September 2026
records.organization: MS Training Centre for Development Cooperation (MS TCDC), Arusha, Tanzania, with the Danida Fellowship Centre (Together for Impact Partnership)
records.overview: Blended youth-leadership fellowship on regional integration in the East African Community region: four weeks of online sessions and two weeks of physical sessions at MS TCDC in Arusha, Tanzania, with mentoring and a regional network. The organiser says it is fully funded under the Together for Impact Partnership between the Danida Fellowship Centre and MS TCDC. The official page lists the Democratic Republic of Congo among the eligible countries; applicants are 18 to 35 with at least a Bachelor's degree. The 4th cohort window (17 August to 7 September 2026) is closed and no later cohort is announced.
records.city: Arusha (MS TCDC campus, physical sessions); online sessions elsewhere
records.program_dates: 4th cohort: event start date 15 November 2026 (YouLead E-Portal). Blended format: online sessions (4 weeks) and physical sessions (2 weeks) at MS TCDC in Arusha, Tanzania.
records.deadline_text: Closed. YouLead E-Portal, 'EAC Youth Fellowship 4th Cohort': 'Open: 17-Aug-2026 02:00 PM', 'Close: 07-Sep-2026 11:59 PM', status 'Application Window Closed'. No time zone is stated. The MS TCDC page still reads 'Apply for the 4th Cohort' but gives no date.
records.expected_next_cycle: No later cohort is announced. The official page and the portal call the closed round the '4th Cohort', which implies earlier cohorts, but no page states when a 5th cohort call will open.
funding_details: MS TCDC FAQ: 'Yes, the EAC Youth Fellowship is fully funded under the Together for Impact Partnership between the Danida Fellowship Centre and MS TCDC.'
'Fellows may also receive a stipend or allowances to cover their expenses during the fellowship period the details of which will be disclosed to selected participants.'
No itemised list of flights, accommodation, meals, visa or insurance is published on the pages read
records.participation_fee: None: the organiser describes the fellowship as fully funded
records.stipend: A stipend or allowances 'may' be paid; details are disclosed to selected participants only
eligibility: Aged 18 to 35
Citizen or resident of Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, South Sudan, Burundi, Rwanda, Somalia or the Democratic Republic of Congo (the page says 'Eligible Countries')
Minimum of a Bachelor's degree or its equivalent
Strong demonstrated leadership potential
Qualifications in regional integration, leadership, business, economic governance or related fields are highly valued
nationality_requirements: Eligible countries listed on the official page: Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, South Sudan, Burundi, Rwanda, Somalia and The Democratic Republic of Congo. The DRC is on the list; the page does not say whether it means citizenship or residence.
records.education_requirement: Minimum of a Bachelor's degree or its equivalent
records.experience_requirement: Strong demonstrated leadership potential is required; no years of experience stated
records.language_requirement: Unknown / Not specified on the pages read
other_requirements: Answer the questions on the application portal
Resume with education, work experience, leadership roles and achievements
Cover letter on interest in regional integration, experience related to the EAC's objectives and motivation
application_process: Apply through the YouLead E-Portal (portal.youlead.africa) when a cohort call is open
Answer the portal questions and upload a resume and a cover letter
Selected fellows join the online sessions (4 weeks) and the physical sessions (2 weeks) in Arusha

records.eligibility_reason: The Democratic Republic of Congo is on the official list of eligible countries, the age range is 18 to 35 and the minimum is a Bachelor's degree, all of which the profile meets. The page also requires 'strong demonstrated leadership potential', which the profile (internships and a field assignment) does not document, and no cohort is open today.
potential_issues: Closed: the 4th cohort window ended on 7 September 2026 and its event started on 15 November 2026; no later cohort is announced
'Strong demonstrated leadership potential is required' and the profile records internships and a field assignment, not leadership roles
Funding is only described as 'fully funded'; flights to Arusha, accommodation, visa and the stipend amount are 'disclosed to selected participants' and not itemised
The programme is run by MS TCDC and the Danida Fellowship Centre, not by the EAC Secretariat; the EAC is its subject
The page says 'Eligible Countries' without saying whether this means citizenship or residence
The portal page listing past cohorts could not be read, so earlier cohort dates are unknown
benefits: Fully funded according to the organiser, with a possible stipend or allowances
Mentoring from experienced mentors and a network of professionals, policymakers and youth leaders across the EAC region
Leadership and policy workshops on regional integration
records.relevance_reason: A fully funded bachelor's-level fellowship whose official country list names the DRC and whose subject (regional integration, economic governance, leadership) is close to the policy-analysis and programme-coordination interests. It is only a watch item until a 5th cohort opens, and the leadership requirement needs real examples.
records.upfront_cost_risk: Low: no fee is mentioned and the organiser says the fellowship is fully funded, but travel and visa costs to Arusha are not itemised
records.action: Do not apply now: the window is closed. Watch the MS TCDC EAC Youth Fellowship page and the YouLead E-Portal list of current opportunities for a 5th cohort call, and meanwhile collect examples of leadership (campaign monitoring, team coordination) for the cover letter.
